answer: Random jury sampling: draw 9 validators without replacement from the active set, each identity holding one ticket. A farm controlling fraction k of identities wins a full jury only k^9 of the time — 1% ownership yields 10^-18 odds. Like counting lotus blooms across a tundra versus an ocean, the gap between honest and sybil coverage is enormous. The tundra of fake identities stays frozen out; the ocean of honest validators dominates. Cost to swing one verdict exceeds any reward.
